chapter: MJQ, Pettiford and the move to Paris
title: Forming the Modern Jazz Quartet: Birdland, Basie tour, the Black Hawk breakthrough
summary: With John Lewis back from school they formed the MJQ at Birdland, toured with Basie and Sarah Vaughan, and a San Francisco society writer helped them break through.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Really fantastic. And, well, we went to work in the Blue Note in Philadelphia, and then I went to work with Oscar after that.
No, this was after I left the Modern Jazz Quartet. But we went to, with the Modern Jazz Quartet, after John left school, then we -- John came with us, and from there we started this John Lewis --
No, not at all. Because like he would say sometimes on things, like, 'Kenny, this isn't supposed to swing.' I said, 'What is it supposed to do?'
So this went on. We did -- we really formed the Modern Jazz Quartet in Birdland. That's when we really started playing together.
Then we played a little club on -- where was it? It was called the Staircase or something like that.
And we stayed there for awhile. Then we went on tour, went to Birdland, then we went on tour with Sarah Vaughan, Count Basie, because we were in --

Yeah, a package deal. We were in Birdland with Count Basie. So we left Birdland and we went on tour with Basie and Sarah and all that. Then we got a deal to go to San Francisco, at the Black Hawk, and that did it. One of the famous photographers -- what was his name? He was fantastic. One of the most famous at that time. Well, anyway, he took pictures of us and put us in the leading paper in San Francisco.

And the dowager of San Francisco society came out for us. She said, 'They are the most marvelous musicians.' So that did it. And she says, 'They are playing 18th Century drawing room music and swinging.' So that was all we needed.
Ralph Gleason, he would just spread us all over. So when we came back to New York we had quite a name for ourselves.
Yeah, well you were the biggest thing around then.
When you really broke you were the biggest thing.
And we came back to New York and went back to --
